title: Workflows
markdown:
**What it is:** Structured, multi-step workflows that produce a *deliverable* — a board deck, a go-to-market plan, a performance review — or *get something done* with your connected tools, like filing emailed bills into a spreadsheet, rather than just a chat reply.

**What it does:**

- Start from **What do you want to get done?** at the top of the page: say what you want done in a sentence, or pick a suggestion chip.
- When you use Open Executive just for yourself, the suggestions and the **Good places to start** picks fit someone running the business alone: a Friday cash and pipeline check, which customers stopped buying, a monthly review, pricing, churn and the quarter's plan. A team sees the board and investor ones.
- Your own workflows sit under **Your workflows** as cards. Each card shows its schedule (or its number of steps) and when it last ran, with a **Run** button and a **⋯** menu (**Edit**, **Delete**). A workflow waiting on a sign-off shows **Waiting for sign-off** and a **Review** button instead, with **Run again** in its **⋯**.
- **Browse N ready-made** opens the ready-made list in a side panel: **Good places to start** first, then a search box and area chips (**All**, **Board**, **Capital**, **Growth & GTM**, **Product**, **People**, **Risk & Legal**, **Operating**, and **System** for the workflows Open Executive runs on its own, like the morning brief).
- Start a run and watch it stream its progress step by step.
- See your runs under **Runs** (in the switch beside **Your workflows**; it shows how many are open), split into **Active**, **Awaiting sign-off**, **Done** and **Error**, grouped by workflow, and search them by name.
- Create your own **custom workflow** by describing it: the assistant asks a few clarifying questions, then drafts it for you to review.
- Let a workflow **use tools** — Gmail, Google Sheets, Drive and anything else connected — to actually do the work, not just write about it.
- Put a custom workflow on a **schedule** (e.g. every Monday at 09:00) so it runs without being asked.
- Each finished run produces a document you can read, copy and download. It is also listed in **Documents**.
- Read and edit **How it's done** on a workflow's page — the method the Executive follows in that workflow and in chat (see **How it's done** in this guide). **Quick** workflows in the ready-made list are one question, one document. A custom workflow's specialist step can **Follow a playbook** too.

**How to use:**

*Run a workflow*

1. Open **Work** in the sidebar (it opens on **Workflows**). Click **Run** on one of your workflows, or click **Browse N ready-made**, narrow the list with the chips or the search box, and click a workflow to open it.
2. The page shows **What it does** (its steps) and **What it needs** (the fields to fill in; required ones have a red \*). **Use example** next to a field, or **Fill with an example** for the whole form, fills in realistic values if you just want to try it.
3. Click **Run it now**, then **Run workflow** (**Back to the details** returns to the form). Progress streams step by step; when it finishes you land on the run page.
4. On the run page, **Copy** copies the document and **Download** offers **Markdown (.md)** or **Word (.docx)**. **Inputs** at the bottom shows what the run was given.

*Who sees a run* — a run you start by hand is visible only to you and to anyone a sign-off in it waits on. Not even the principal sees a teammate's own run. Scheduled and system runs belong to the team: everyone signed in to the workspace sees them. A few system workflows can only be started by the principal (the weekly review, and the morning brief when you use Open Executive just for yourself).

*Manage runs* — each run's **⋯** under **Runs** has **Delete run** (you are asked to confirm). A group shows its five newest runs; **Show N more** lists the rest. A failed scheduled run has **Run again** on its page, which the principal or the person it delivers to can use; it delivers the way the scheduled run would have. **Start a new run instead** opens the workflow's form.

*Build your own*

1. Under **What do you want to get done?**, describe the job in plain words — what it should produce, who it's for, and how often — or pick one of the suggestions, then click **Start**. (The **⋯** beside **Start** has **New workflow**, which opens the same conversation empty, **New workflow, step by step**, which opens the advanced editor, and **Talk it through in chat**, which starts a chat.)
2. Answer the clarifying questions (usually two or three) by typing or by clicking a suggested answer. **Draft it now** skips the rest.
3. Review the draft: its steps, schedule, what you fill in each run, the assumptions it made, and the **tools** each action step will use (ones that can change things are listed under *Creating this workflow lets it use these tools*).
4. Click **Create workflow** — this approves those tools, and runs use them without asking again — or **Keep refining** and type what to change, or **Edit details** to fine-tune it field by field in the advanced editor. It appears under **Your workflows**.

The signed-in person who creates a workflow becomes its owner: they are the one asked when it wants to write somewhere new (see below).

*Change a custom workflow* — **Edit** in its **⋯**, or **Change it** on its page, opens a conversation. Say what to change in your own words (who signs off, when it runs, what a step does). It shows **Proposed changes** next to **How it works now**, and nothing is saved until you click **Save changes**. If the change adds tools that can change things, saving approves them. **Use the advanced editor** opens the form instead. **Delete** in the **⋯** removes the workflow after a confirmation; this cannot be undone.

*Advanced editor* — reached from **New workflow, step by step** in the **⋯** beside **Start**, **Edit details** on a draft, or **Use the advanced editor**. It has four stages; move between them with **Next** and **Back**, and **Cancel** to leave:

1. **Details:** a unique **Name** in snake_case (e.g. `weekly_competitor_watch`; 3–49 lowercase letters, digits or underscores, starting with a letter, and not starting with `quick_`; it can't be changed later), a **Title**, **Description**, **Section** and **Estimated minutes** (1–120).
2. **Input fields:** click **+ Add field** for anything the person running it must supply, with a **Field name**, **Label** and a **Required** tick. Remove one with **Remove field** in its **⋯**. Use a field in a step's goal as `{field_name}`.
3. **Steps:** add **+ Specialist** steps (pick a specialist, write its goal, optionally **Follow a playbook**), **+ Action** steps (write what to get done and where, then **Search tools** and **+ Add** the ones it may use), and, if someone must sign off, an **+ Approval gate** (who to ask, the question, a timeout, and what happens on timeout: `escalate`, `auto_proceed` or `fail`). New steps are added at the bottom. Use **Move up** / **Move down** in a step's **⋯** to place them above the synthesis step, which pulls everything together and must stay last; put an approval gate just before it. **Remove step** deletes one. Up to 12 steps and 16 input fields.
4. **Schedule (optional):** tick **Run on a schedule**, enter a **Cadence**, and pick who the document is delivered to under **Deliver document to**. A scheduled workflow can't have required input fields or approval gates.
5. Click **Create workflow** (**Save changes** when editing).

Cadences are written like this (times are UTC): `daily@09:00`, `weekly@mon@09:00`, or `quarterly@01-09:00` (the 1st of January, April, July and October).

*Workflows that use tools* — describe the job and where things live, e.g. *"Every morning, find the bills I email you, read each PDF and add a row (vendor, amount, due date) to my Bill tracker sheet."* The assistant finds the right tools (here Gmail search and attachments, reading PDFs, and appending rows to Google Sheets) and asks about anything it needs, like which sheet. While a run works, the progress list shows the tool each action step is using, and the step's result ends with **Actions taken**. A workflow can only use the tools you approved, and every tool call is recorded in the audit log. You can also ask for one in chat: a workflow that uses tools is saved **switched off**, and the Executive gives you a link. It shows as **Waiting for your approval** at the top of **Your workflows**; click **Review**, check the steps and tools, and click **Turn on workflow**. Until then it can't run or follow a schedule.

*Signing off a paused run* — when a run reaches an approval gate it moves to **Awaiting sign-off** and the approver is messaged on their usual channel. They answer by replying on Slack, Discord or Telegram — "yes", "LGTM", "no", "not now" — or with **Approve** / **Decline** on the run page. Only the person the run waits on, or the principal, can answer. "No" or "not now" ends the run. If nobody answers before the timeout, the gate's timeout rule applies.

*The first write somewhere new* — a workflow that uses tools picks where to write each time it runs (this month's tab, the sender of an invoice, a new doc per client). The first time it wants to write somewhere it hasn't written before — a different spreadsheet, a new recipient — that one write waits, the rest of the run carries on, and the workflow's owner is asked: yes lets it write there now and in future runs, no skips it. The places a workflow may write without asking are listed under **Approved targets** on its page; **Remove** one and it asks again.

**From chat:**

- *"What workflows can you run?"* or *"Run a competitive teardown of Acme."* — the Executive runs it and brings the result back into the conversation.
- *"Build me a workflow called weekly_competitor_watch: the CMO checks our top three competitors for pricing and product changes, then summarise. Run it every Monday at 09:00 UTC and send it to me."* — the Executive drafts it, shows you a summary, and saves it once you say yes.

*Note: outputs are listed in Documents. Ask OE can also fill in the advanced editor form for you.*
